original.description: ERS-EO Proof of Concept on Critical Infrastructure ManagementThe ERS-EO Element 1 Critical Infrastructure Monitoring Prof of Concept is intended to demonstrate the step improvement for enhanced monitoring and management of critical infrastructure resulting from the effective combination of diverse EO and non-EO capabilities representative of the future Earth Observation Governmental Service (EOGS) capacity.  In particular, the customization and fusion of these capabilities will generate significant improvements in tasking response, persistent data collection, information delivery latency, expanded information content andflexibility and adaptability in response to dynamic situations. In this context, the Critical Infrastructure Monitoring PoC will:Stimulate innovative combinations of public and private EO systems to support improved and more flexible tasking, response latency, persistence and cross-operator cueing;Develop customized workflows connecting satellite operators, non-EO data providers, analytics tool developers and critical infrastructure operators to ensure enhanced capability to detect, characterize, respond to and mitigateemergent threats and anomalies;Verify the improvements achievable over current state of the art with respect to emerging threat detection and mitigation action execution for critical infrastructure operators under realistic operating conditions;With respect to gaps in current capabilities, elaborate technical approaches for their resolution, verify their impact under representative operational environments and conditionsand elaborate a road map for eventual transfer to full operations based on exclusively European technology. The contract will integrate existing EO and non-EO capabilities as well as capabilities at an advanced stage of development into a pre-operational network providing a range of analysis support information. The procurement will be structured into three periods as follows:Step[BJ1]  1:requirements consolidation and initial operating capability specification, implementation and testing.Step 2 initial capability demonstrations under realistic operating conditions covering extended routine threat mitigation, timely detection, characterization and response elaboration for emerging threats and anomaly/event response situationsStep 3: extended capability demonstration under fully representative conditions as agreed in the milestone review concluding Step 2 activities All underlying Information and Communication Technology (ICT) functions will be provided by the ERS-EO Element 1 Testbed.

original.description: This feasibility study shall analyse Canadian space weather assets including measurement, modelling and service provision capabilities and carry out initial pre-developments demonstrating these assets potential incorporation into the ESA Space Weather Service Network. Assets providing data access to be reviewed shall include both space and ground-based sensors along with data archives and repositories.Available assets shall be reviewed in terms of the Space Safety Programme's space weather customer and service requirements baseline along with the current level of service provided by the existing Space Weather Service Network in order to highlight priority areas where Canadian assets are expected to bring substantial capability enhancements. Consideration shall be given to the development planning prepared by the five Expert Service Centres participating in the network to ensure complementarity.Recommendations shall include identification of a set of high priority product development activities in key areas highlighting the potential contribution of Canadian space weather assets and capabilities both alone and in combination with other existing or potential SWE Service Network participants. Predevelopment shall take place in order to produce a set of representative product mock-ups. The first products shall be foreseen for integration into the SWE Service Network within the 2026 timeframe.

original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, build and test a highly integrated and efficient millimetre-wave phased array antenna using advanced packaging solution for multi-chip,multi-technology assembly, including 3-dimensional heterogeneous integration interconnects, thermal and power management.Targeted Improvements:Enabling disruptive technology to enable thermal management of highly integrated phased arrays, with a twice the RF power handling capability.Description: The development and deployment of millimetre-wave phased array antennas present several challenges that can reduce their efficiency and performance. These challenges include low RF power per element across different orbits (Low Earth Orbit (LEO), Medium Earth Orbit (MEO), and Geostationary EarthOrbit (GEO)) due to the use of silicon chips and the inefficiency in thermal management. Further limitations are introduced by the use of 2D packaging, which prevents the integration of high-power handling capabilities and enhanced thermal management technologies.The power efficiency and dependability of the antenna are reduced by signal strength degradation caused by the low RF output power per element. These performance issues directly affect satellite-to-ground communication as well as intersatellite communication.Toovercome these limitations, transitioning from 2D to 3D Heterogeneous Integration (3DHI) interconnect technology can significantly improve the thermal and power performance of phased array antennas. By stacking components vertically, more space can be allocated for effective thermal management, and the integration of multiple layers with thermal vias allows for better heat dissipation. This approach also enables the integration of diverse materials and technologies within the same package. Novel materials like Gallium Nitride (GaN) and Silicon Carbide (SiC) offer superior thermal conductivity and higher power handling capabilities compared to traditional silicon. Incorporating thesematerials into the antenna array, using an Integrated Antenna-on-Chip (AoC) approach, can increase the RF power per element while alleviating thermal constraints.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 will develop an antenna concept, investigate and develop key processes necessary to fabricate a millimetre-wave 3DHI active antenna.This includes integrating low-power silicon chips, RF power amplifiers, thermal management solutions and advanced packaging techniques. During this phase, critical components will be developed to breadboard level to assess the effectiveness of 3D packaging methods, such as vertical integration and thermal vias, in addressing thermal dissipation and RF power handling challenges. Phase 1 outputwill deliver an antenna concept supported by critical breadboard test results. The budget for Phase 1 is up to 1,000 kEuro.- Phase2 will focus on developing a scaled engineering model of a millimetre-wave phased array antenna using 3DHI technology in Q, V, orW-Bands. Phase 2 will include refining the design, manufacturing, and testing the antenna's performance in representative operational environments.

original.description: A new approach to engineering, sustaining and third-level maintenance is proposed for the Back-End installations at the Deep Spacesites in New Norcia, Cebreros, and Malarge, the Near-Earth sites in Kiruna and Kourou, and the Ground Station Reference Facility(GSRF) at ESOC. Under this approach, following a successful phase-in, the end-to-end responsibility for these installations shall betaken over by the prime contractor. The term Back-End refers in the ESTRACK terminology to the systems integrating the Tracking,Telemetry, Command Processor, the ground systems test and validation infrastructure, Frequency and Timing subsystem and the IT infrastructure of the ground stations. The contractual scope of this procurement proposal includes integration and sustaining activities, predictive and corrective maintenance of the various backend subsystems and subsystem retests, spares and repair procurement and third-level support to the Maintenance and Operations (MO) teams for all ESTRACK terminals.
